{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
#flux: -n {{:ncpus}}
#flux: -t {{:wallhr}}h
#
# NOTE: PBS -P np01 (project/account) has no direct portable Flux batch directive here.
# Omitting it may affect job priority/accounting and queue wait time (performance as time-to-solution).
#
# NOTE: PBS -q normal (queue) has no direct portable Flux batch directive here.
# Omitting it may affect queue wait time and/or scheduling policy (performance as time-to-solution).
#
# NOTE: PBS -N "{{:name}}" (job name) has no direct portable Flux batch directive included here.
# Omitting it has no runtime performance impact, but makes job identification/monitoring less convenient.
#
# NOTE: PBS -l mem={{:mem}}GB has no direct portable Flux batch directive included here.
# Omitting it may impact performance or stability if the job exceeds default memory limits (possible OOM/eviction).
#
# NOTE: PBS -j oe (join stdout/stderr) has no direct portable Flux batch directive included here.
# Omitting it has no runtime performance impact, but stdout/stderr handling will use Flux defaults.

source "$HOME/hpc-environments/gadi/load-intel.sh"
PROJECT_DIR="$SCRATCH/{{:dir_name}}/"

# Use Flux launcher instead of mpiexec to respect Flux allocation.
flux run -n {{:ncpus}} julia --project="$PROJECT_DIR" --check-bounds no -O3 \
    "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/Benchmarks/benchmark_gadi.jl" \
    "{{:name}}" \
    "{{{:write_dir}}}" \
    "{{:type}}" \
    "{{:bmark_type}}" \
    "{{:Nx_partition}}" \
    "{{:Ny_partition}}" \
    "{{:Nz_partition}}" \
    "{{:n_el_size}}" \
    "{{:fe_order}}" \
    "{{:verbose}}" \
    "{{:nreps}}"
"
}
